walkthroughs.body_html:
A wave carries energy without moving matter overall.

Picture a rope wiggled at one end. The wiggle (energy) travels to the other end, but the rope itself stays roughly where it was.

That's the big idea: energy travels, matter stays put.

Every wave has the same parts. The wavelength (symbol λ) is the distance from one peak to the next, measured in metres.

The amplitude is how tall the wave gets from rest — bigger amplitude means more energy.

The frequency is how many waves pass per second, measured in hertz (Hz).

Transverse waves wobble at right angles to the direction of travel. Light, water ripples and rope waves are all transverse.

Longitudinal waves wobble back-and-forth in the same direction as travel — they have squashed bits (compressions) and stretched bits (rarefactions). Sound is the classic example. 🔊

mcqs.q: Which type of wave is a sound wave?
options: Transverse
Longitudinal
Surface only
Electromagnetic

mcqs.q: Which property of a wave is measured in hertz (Hz)?
options: Wavelength
Amplitude
Frequency
Wave speed

mcqs.q: When a wave travels through water, what happens to the water itself?
options: The water moves along with the wave from one place to another.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
The water turns into wave material and changes state.
The water oscillates about a fixed point; the wave transfers energy, not matter.

mcqs.q: What property of a sound wave determines its pitch?
options: Amplitude determines pitch — a bigger wave is a higher-pitched note.
The water turns into wave material and changes state.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.
The frequency — higher frequency means higher pitch.

mcqs.q: How do you see a non-luminous object like a book?
options: Light from a source reflects off the book and enters your eyes.
Your eyes send out beams of vision that hit the book and let you see it.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
The water turns into wave material and changes state.
